candidates.description: Triggers when the user invokes `/gtm-context` or explicitly asks to create, import, update, delete, validate, or repair a plain Markdown GTM context repository at `~/.gtm/<org-slug>/`. This includes adding teammates or suborganizations, refreshing stored facts, maintaining the repository’s minimal contract, and fixing its Git health. The requested outcome must change or administer the context repository itself; merely reading, inspecting, or depending on existing context is insufficient. Excludes defining ICPs or personas, account/lead segmentation, scoring or research, CRM administration, ordinary Git repositories or folders, and non-GTM knowledge bases.
candidates.rationale: Best balance of recall and precision. It preserves every positive class while adding a strong outcome-based gate that directly blocks the observed segmentation false positive.

candidates.description: Triggers when the user invokes `/gtm-context` or requests lifecycle or maintenance work on a plain Markdown GTM context repository at `~/.gtm/<org-slug>/`: creating, importing, updating, deleting, validating, or repairing it; adding teammates or suborganizations; refreshing facts; or restoring its minimal contract or Git health. It does not trigger when the repository is only a read-only source or dependency for another task. Excludes ICP/persona definition, account or lead segmentation, scoring and research, CRM administration, ordinary Git work, and non-GTM knowledge bases.
candidates.rationale: Compact and highly explicit about read-only dependency. “Lifecycle or maintenance work” neatly unifies the positive cases without broadening into downstream GTM analysis.

candidates.description: Triggers when the user invokes `/gtm-context` or asks for a direct change to, or integrity check of, a plain Markdown GTM context repository at `~/.gtm/<org-slug>/`, including create, import, update, delete, validate, repair, teammate or suborganization additions, fact refreshes, minimal-contract maintenance, and Git-health repair. Using existing context as input—even when the task requires inspecting it—does not qualify. Excludes ICPs, personas, account/lead segmentation, scoring or research, CRM administration, general Git repositories or folders, and non-GTM knowledge bases.
candidates.rationale: Uses the sharpest anti-false-positive wording by stating that even required inspection does not qualify. It is slightly more abstract than the first two because “direct change” and “integrity check” summarize the trigger boundary.
